bug_semantics: CWE-416 use-after-free of a function pointer in miSyncDestroyFence(). When a fence is destroyed, the function sets sync.beingDestroyed and walks pFence->sync.pTriglist, invoking each trigger's CounterDestroyed callback (SyncAwaitTriggerFired for Await) before capturing ptl->next and freeing the list node. CounterDestroyed can FreeResource the Await, and FreeAwait then frees the entire SyncAwaitUnion for that Await group while skipping SyncDeleteTriggerFromSyncObject because beingDestroyed is already set. If one Await has multiple conditions on the same fence, later SyncTriggerList nodes still hold pTrigger pointers into the freed union; the next iteration performs (*ptl->pTrigger->CounterDestroyed) on dangling memory. A local client can Await a fence with multiple triggers, then a second connection DestroyFence to crash the server or escalate if it runs as root.
flaw_origin: The unsafe destroy loop was first written when fence sync objects were added in 2010. 1c4a0db2c6bf0320cb630b84ab87bcfd3801a53d introduced miSyncDestroyFence() by copying FreeCounter()'s already-present pattern: call CounterDestroyed, then read ptl->next and free the node, with a copy-pasted comment about the 'counter' being destroyed. FreeAwait already left trigger-list nodes in place and freed the Await union when beingDestroyed was set, so multiple same-object Await conditions were already a UAF. Later commits only restyled or indented the loop (9838b7032ea9792bec21af424c53c07078636d21, 7f962c70b6d9c346477f23f6c15211e749110078); they did not first write the mechanism.
